summary: The difference between how things are today and how they should be.
example: Today the depot finds one fault in five and buyers find the rest. The aim is for the depot to find most faults, before produce leaves.
definition: A gap is the difference between how things are now and how they should be, in results. It names a result that falls short, not a missing tool, budget or method. A KPI can track it: its baseline is how things are now and its target is how they should be. A gap lists where it was seen, such as which regions. Projects and programmes that work on it name it in their problems, and one or more outcomes say what will be true once it is closed. A gap is not a problem (what the gap does to a group of people), not an outcome, not a missing resource, and not a KPI.

cues.gap: a problem today compared with where it should be

/metadata/name.guide: A short name for what is wrong, not the work that would fix it.

poor.why: Names the fix, not what is wrong.
A topic, not a shortfall: it says neither what is wrong nor where.
A gap in resources, not in results: say what the missing scanners cause, such as faults found after dispatch.

/spec/measure.guide: The KPI that tracks this gap. Its baseline is how things are now and its target is how they should be. Leave it empty if no KPI tracks it yet; do not make up a number.
good: post-harvest-loss-rate, for the gap Too much harvest is lost after picking: its baseline of 18 percent is where things are, its target of 9 percent is where they should be.

poor.text: member-season-earnings, for the gap Faults are found after dispatch
poor.why: Earnings change for many reasons, so this KPI does not track this gap.

poor.text: quality-pass-rate, while also writing 62 and 75 into the current and desired states
poor.why: The KPI already has these numbers. Do not write them twice.

/spec/current.guide: How things are now, as something you can see happening. Leave it empty if a KPI tracks this gap.
good: One fault in five is found at intake; buyers find the rest.
Each depot checks against its own checklist.

poor.why: Too vague to tell when it has changed: say what is observed, and where.

poor.text: Depots lack trained staff and scanners.
poor.why: Names what is missing, not the result. Say what happens, such as faults reaching buyers.

/spec/desired.guide: How things should be, as something you will be able to see. Leave it empty if a KPI tracks this gap.
good: Most faults are found at intake, before produce leaves the depot.
Every depot checks against one published standard.

poor.text: Train every depot supervisor in the standard.
poor.why: This is something to do. Say what would be true once it worked.
Does not say how things should be. Describe it.

/spec/affects.guide: The groups of people this shortfall falls on. A problem that cites this gap names its groups from these, so the two always describe the same people.
good: member-growers, for the gap Faults are found after dispatch

/spec/outcomes.guide: The outcomes that will be true once this gap is closed. If none fits, add one under its objective first.
good: faults-found-before-dispatch, for the gap Faults are found after dispatch
depot-staff-apply-the-standard-alike, for the gap No single quality standard

poor.why: A goal, not an outcome. Pick an outcome.
An objective, not an outcome. Pick the outcome under it that says what will be true.

/spec/segments.guide: Where the gap was seen, such as which regions or product lines. Pick the specific ones, not just the category.
good: northern-region and southern-region, for a review that found faults reaching buyers in both
fresh-produce and dried-produce, as values of product-line

poor.why: Names the category, not which regions. Pick the regions where the gap was seen.
A group of people the work is for, not a part where the gap was seen.

/spec/source.guide: The document and section where this gap was written down.
good: Quality review of the 2025 spring season, section 2
Quality review of the 2025 spring season, section 4

poor.why: Not precise enough to find again: which season, which section?
A role, not a document. Name the document with what they reported.

/spec/statement.guide: The finding word for word from the source. Do not change it.
good: Four in five quality faults are found by a buyer rather than at intake.
Each depot keeps its own checklist and none of them agree.

poor.why: A recommendation, not the finding, and not the source's words.

poor.text: Four in five quality faults in the northern region are found by a buyer.
poor.why: The quote was changed. Copy it word for word.

/spec/note.guide: Anything else to know about the finding, such as how it was counted.
good: Counted by hand during the review; no system holds the checklists, so this cannot be watched yet.

poor.text: The quality check rollout is fixing this.
poor.why: Record the work on the project or programme instead, by naming this gap in its problem.

/spec/dataSources.guide: Where the data on this gap comes from. Leave it empty if nothing records it.

Project:/spec/summary/problems/-/gaps/-/.ask: Which project works on this gap, and in which parts? Its problem names this gap and the parts it covers.
Project:/spec/summary/problems/-/gaps/-/.ifNone: Nothing to add now. When a project takes on this gap, name the gap in its problem.

Programme:/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/gap.ask: Which programme works on this gap, and in which parts? Its problem names this gap and the parts it covers.
Programme:/spec/problems/-/gaps/-/gap.ifNone: Nothing to add now. When a programme takes on this gap, name the gap in its problem.

checks.gap-states: Say how things are now and how they should be, or pick a KPI that tracks this gap.
checks.gap-outcome: Name the outcome that would be true once the gap is closed, defining it under its objective first if there is none.
checks.gap-measured: Pick the KPI that tracks this gap. If there is none yet, describe how things are now and how they should be, and name the source.
checks.gap-source: Name the document and section the finding was written down in.
checks.gap-segments: Name the specific parts where the gap was seen, such as which regions.
checks.gap-covered: Name this gap in the problem of each project or programme that works on it, with the parts it covers.
checks.gap-results: Say which result falls short, not which resource or method is missing.

good.label: a result that falls short of where it should be

poor.label: a missing resource, tool, budget or method

gap-results.fail: Reads as a missing resource or method: say which result falls short, and by how much.
